newsitem.title: UK: BA says fuel costs limit profits rise.
newsitem.headline: BA says fuel costs limit profits rise.

text.p: British Airways Plc announced a 9.3 percent rise in first-half pretax profits to 470 million pounds ($769.6 million) on Tuesday, but said they could have been even higher were it not for the leap in fuel prices this year.

The airline said continued strong traffic growth and greater productivity would have boosted operating profits by 10.5 percent had it not been for an extra 51 million pounds on its fuel bill and the impact of a threatened pilots strike in July.
In the event first-half operating profits were down by 2.1 percent on a year ago to 512 million pounds.

"The economic outlook for the main countries in which we operate remains generally encouraging with forecasts of continued steady growth in supply and demand," chairman Sir Colin Marshall said in his results statement.

But chief executive Robert Ayling said the rise in oil prices along with some increase in flying pushed BA's fuel and oil costs up by a third so far this year and warned that further increases in air fares could be on the way.

"It's for each individual airline of course to take their decisions on this but I think some of these costs we can expect to see coming out in increased fares in due course," he told Reuters in a post-results interview.
"I think all the airlines have been taken by surprise. I would be surprised if you found many airline managers who guessed it correctly before Christmas last year. We didn't."

BA said it flew a record 20 million passengers in the half year with passenger traffic up 4.6 percent and sold an average of 75.2 percent of available seats per flight. This was down by 1.7 percentage points on a year ago but it had increased capacity by 6.8 percent in the same period.
